title: Chinese frontier AI models carry the fingerprint of export-controlled GPUs
lede: Will DePue's forensic report says six recent models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group were initialised on export-controlled Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, judging by traces in their published weights.

points: PyTorch spreads random weight initialisation across GPU threads, and the thread count depends on how many streaming multiprocessors the chip has.
Recovering the seed and thread layout from untouched weights reveals the hardware class: Hopper at 132 SMs, Blackwell at 148 or 152.
Earlier models from the same labs read as Hopper, as do the newest from Alibaba, Zhipu, Tencent, Xiaomi and StepFun.
The method agreed with all 24 models whose builders disclosed their hardware, and the matches sit far above chance.
The report says it cannot show where the chips were located or whether export controls were broken.

points.text: The most common reply: renting Nvidia GPUs in data centers outside China, such as Singapore or Malaysia, is legal under current rules.
One commenter doubts the author's neutrality and notes no code was published; a reply says they confused DePue with someone else.
Readers ask whether matching the initialisation proves the training itself ran on the same hardware.
A technical aside: the Muon optimizer tends to erase initial weight patterns, though untouched rows remain strong evidence.
Several argue export controls rarely hold, citing reseller chains and minimal identity checks at cloud GPU hosts.
